sources: dossier=Net position: two settlement modes, aggregate is 'claim-chain aggregation'; design corpus=claim-tree.md 'only once every claim-holder row on the parent and every child claim-handle row is no longer active does it compute the parent's aggregate verdict per its snapshotted aggregation policy'; doc=child-execution.md:16 previously read as if the policy decides WHEN the parent settles and partition contexts close incrementally; code=child_execution.go SettleFromFanoutChild:288-334 returns early on any active holder/child, aggregateParentOutcome (488-523) runs only once the gate passes, close loop (337-369) closes all children together
note: claim-tree.md (design corpus, already corrected) independently states the same all-non-active gate the code implements; child-execution.md's aggregate-settle bullet misattributed timing to the policy. Rewrote the bullet to match: policy is evaluated once the gate passes, closing all partition contexts together in that firing.

sources: dossier=silent on this specific ownership line; design corpus=claim-tree.md:17 'Does NOT own: claim acquisition (see concept:claim, concept:claim-handle)', fan-out.md:19 owns 'the partition-split mechanics at parent-acquisition' and fan-out.md invariant 'Sub-claim acquisition happens upstream of dispatch... per concept:child-execution'; doc=child-execution.md:26 previously attributed sub-claim acquisition to concept:claim-tree; code=runner_subclaim.go AcquireSubClaims sits upstream of dispatch, claim-tree code owns only the parent pointer and recursive walks
note: claim-tree.md explicitly disowns claim acquisition and fan-out.md explicitly owns the partition-split/sub-claim-acquisition mechanics; child-execution.md's Boundaries line pointed at the wrong neighbor concept. Corrected the citation from claim-tree to fan-out.

sources: dossier=Net position (untiered, no date/hash/transcript citation) 'settlement is the only run-side path that closes child execution contexts (instance termination is the administrative exception)'; design corpus=run-scope.md invariant 'A closed RunScope means parent-run rendezvous has fired ... or the owning frame has ended (root)' — no third administrative-exception path documented, and root RunScopes are explicitly not child execution contexts (sub-graph/fanout_partition) per run-scope.md's own three-kind taxonomy; doc=child-execution.md:30 parenthetical 'instance termination is the administrative exception, per concept:run-scope'; code=lifecycle.go CloseAndFanOutFrameRootRunScopesForInstance:289-343 closes only f.RootRunScopeID (single-row, no child cascade) per frame — never a sub-graph or fanout_partition scope; postgres run_scopes.go Close:73 is single-row with no cascade
note: The finding's factual claims are confirmed: run-scope.md documents no instance-termination exception and the admin path only ever closes frame ROOT scopes, which by run-scope.md's own taxonomy are not child execution contexts at all. The dossier's parenthetical is an untiered Net-position assertion, uncorroborated elsewhere and design-incoherent with run-scope.md's own (already-corrected) invariant. Flagging suspect-canonization: is 'instance termination is the administrative exception' a real intended closure path that code/run-scope.md simply haven't caught up to, or is this stale phrasing that should be dropped from child-execution.md entirely?

sources: dossier=silent on multi-exit validation specifics; design corpus=delegation.md invariant 'The delegate target MUST be a sub-graph (with both entry and exit declared)...' (exit treated as singular throughout, no multi-exit rejection mentioned); doc=child-execution.md:32 previously claimed 'if a delegate target declared more than one exit, template validation rejects it'; code=spec/graphs.go:13 GraphSpec.Exit is a scalar string (unrepresentable to declare >1), template_validator_graphs.go rejects only missing exit (subgraph_missing_exit), entry==exit (subgraph_entry_equals_exit), and unknown exit (subgraph_unknown_exit) — no multi-exit rejection exists or is needed
note: The template grammar makes a second exit unrepresentable (Exit is a single scalar field), so no validation-rejection code path for 'more than one exit' exists or could fire; delegation.md corroborates by treating exit as singular throughout. Rewrote the invariant to describe the actual mechanism: single-exit is enforced structurally by the grammar shape, not by a runtime validation rejection.
